questions.question: Describe how the empire of Mali was founded and explain how historians should treat the Epic of Sundiata as a source.
questions.expected_answer: Sundiata Keita united the Mande clans after defeating Sumanguru Kante of the Sosso at the Battle of Kirina in about 1235 and became the first mansa. The epic is an oral tradition passed down by griots; it is valuable evidence but was designed to praise and inspire, so legendary details should be checked against other sources such as Arabic writings and archaeology.

questions.question: Give four sources of Mali's wealth at its height.
questions.expected_answer: Gold from Bambuk and Bure, with the mansa keeping all nuggets; taxes on trade, especially salt, copper and gold; agriculture and fishing on the Niger floodplains; tribute from conquered and allied peoples; crafts.

questions.question: Explain two ways in which Mali was governed effectively, and why the Catalan Atlas is useful evidence about Mansa Musa.
questions.expected_answer: The mansa was ruler, judge and commander; provinces were run by appointed officials or by local kings who stayed loyal and paid tribute; a strong army kept roads safe; Muslim scholars kept records and advised. The Catalan Atlas (about 1375) is a European primary source showing that Mansa Musa's wealth was known in Europe, depicting him with a gold nugget.
